source.title: The basal ganglia: focused selection and inhibition of competing motor programs

confidence_rationale: Mink's center-surround model is the canonical statement of the exact selection STRUCTURE ARC-107 imports: the basal ganglia do not generate movement; they broadly INHIBIT competing motor programs (the surround / No-Go) while focally REMOVING inhibition from the selected one (the center / Go via disinhibition). This is precisely 'an upstream signal's strength is necessary but not sufficient -- it also needs lawful access' (design note s1): access is granted by focal disinhibition, denied to competitors by surround inhibition. It grounds MECH-449's bounded-Go-plus-bounded-No-Go constitution AND the pallidal-permission-gate framing (a winner is the one whose inhibition is released, not the one with the highest scalar). Held below 0.8 because it is a conceptual review (not a single decisive experiment) and its currency is motor programs, not abstract committed-action classes; and because the surround-inhibition idea has been partly contested downstream (the strict center-surround anatomy is debated even if the focused-selection function is robust).
failure_signatures: Mink's selection works by REMOVING tonic inhibition from the chosen program and INCREASING it on competitors; REE's argmin has no tonic-inhibition / permission layer at all -- the committed action is simply the lowest-J candidate, so there is nothing to 'release' and no surround to suppress competitors. The model names exactly the missing machinery ARC-107 must build (permission gate + No-Go surround), so a selector that only sharpens the scalar will not reproduce the function.

If the focal-release signal itself is driven by the same dominant scalar (F), then the 'center' is always F's argmax and the surround always suppresses the non-F channels -- the diversity ceiling reappears in the gating layer. Mink's function only yields behavioural flexibility if the center can be set by a channel OTHER than the monopolising score; this is the same residual-ceiling risk MECH-448 targets, relocated to the disinhibition step.

The model is about preventing UNWANTED movements (surround inhibition stops interference), not about maximising committed-action DIVERSITY; importing it naively could over-suppress and NARROW the repertoire (the bradykinesia/over-No-Go failure mode) rather than widening it -- the psychiatric failure-mode column must track this both-directions risk.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The basal ganglia do not generate movement. When voluntary movement is generated by cortical and cerebellar mechanisms, the basal ganglia act broadly to inhibit competing motor programs that would otherwise interfere with the desired movement, while focally removing inhibition from the desired program so it can proceed. Inability to inhibit competing programs produces slow movements, abnormal postures, and involuntary muscle activity.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-107 reframes the conversion-ceiling as a selection-STRUCTURE fault: a formed signal reaches E3 authority but committed action does not change, because the selector is `candidates -> scalar dominance -> argmin` with no eligibility/permission layer. Mink's focused-selection model is the canonical reference for the layer ARC-107 adds: a pallidal-like PERMISSION gate that works by releasing focal inhibition from the eligible action (MECH-448's 'within-eligible arbitration wins access') while a bounded No-Go SURROUND suppresses competitors (MECH-449's bounded No-Go pressure). Critically, Mink makes explicit that the selected action is the one whose inhibition is RELEASED -- not the one with the highest input scalar -- which is exactly the argmin-vs-permission distinction at the heart of ARC-107.
mapping.mapping_caveat: ANALOGY-LEVEL, conceptual-review grounding. Mink's units are motor programs with literal tonic GABAergic inhibition (SNr/GPi); REE has no tonic-inhibition substrate and its 'programs' are abstract committed-action classes, so 'release inhibition' becomes 'admit to the eligible set / grant commit permission' -- a functional, not mechanical, translation. The strict center-surround ANATOMY has been partially contested downstream even where the focused-selection FUNCTION is robust, so the import is of the function (focal-go + surround-no-go), explicitly not the literal anatomical wiring. And the model is framed around PREVENTING interference, so a naive import risks over-suppression (repertoire narrowing) rather than the diversity recovery ARC-107 wants -- a both-directions failure mode the falsifier and the psychiatric column must track.
mapping.source_context: Comprehensive theoretical review in Progress in Neurobiology integrating BG circuitry, single-unit activity during movement, and lesion effects; one of the most-cited statements of the BG focused-selection / surround-inhibition hypothesis.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high for a conceptual synthesis (canonical, heavily cited, integrates physiology + lesion + anatomy) but it is a review-level argument, not a decisive single experiment, so capped below the empirical papers. Mapping fidelity good on the selection STRUCTURE (focal-go + surround-no-go + release-not-argmax) which is the exact ARC-107 import. Transfer risk moderate: motor-program currency and literal tonic inhibition do not exist in REE, so the translation is functional; plus the contested anatomy means I weight the function, not the wiring.
